blocks.content: "Docker Engine" is the name for the whole client-server application that makes Docker work: the client, the REST API between them, and the daemon, bundled together as one product.

It is easy to use "Docker" and "the daemon" interchangeably, but strictly, Docker Engine is the complete package: the docker CLI (client), the REST API that connects client to daemon, and dockerd (the daemon) itself. When you install Docker on a Linux server, "Docker Engine" is what you are installing.

blocks.alt: Engine is the client, the API, and the daemon, together

blocks.content: Docker Engine itself is only the top of a taller stack. Your command flows from the client, through the daemon, down into containerd, down further into runc, which finally talks to the host kernel to actually create the isolated process. Each layer has a narrower, more specific job than the one above it.

blocks.alt: Each layer hands off to a more specialized one below it

blocks.content: 3. The REST API Is the Real Interface
blocks.text: 3. The REST API Is the Real Interface

blocks.content: The CLI is not special, it is just one consumer of Docker's REST API. Anything the CLI can do, you could do yourself with a raw HTTP request to that same API, and that is exactly what Docker Desktop's GUI and every Docker SDK (Python, Go, and others) actually do under the hood.

blocks.alt: The CLI is one client among several for the same API

blocks.content:
curl --unix-socket /var/run/docker.sock http://localhost/containers/json
# Same information "docker ps" shows you, fetched directly
# from the REST API the CLI itself talks to.

blocks.content: On Linux, Docker Engine runs natively since the kernel features it needs are already there. On Mac and Windows, there is no Linux kernel to share, so Docker Desktop quietly runs a small Linux virtual machine in the background and installs Docker Engine inside it, giving you the same experience on top of a very different underlying setup.

blocks.alt: Servers run Engine directly, desktops run it inside a small VM

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Docker Engine is the umbrella name for the client, the REST API, and the daemon together, not just the daemon alone.
The CLI is just one of several possible clients for the same underlying REST API, which is why GUI tools and SDKs can do everything the CLI can.
